title: 3.5.5 Lab: Read and Update Object Fields
description: Build one object, read a field with a dot, change a field, add a new field, and print the object. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Create the object
steps.instructions: Create a variable named book and assign it an object literal with at least two properties, for example a title and a pages count.

steps.title: Read a field with a dot
steps.instructions: Use console.log and dot notation to print one of the object's properties.

steps.title: Change a field
steps.instructions: Assign a new value to one of the properties that already exists on the object. Use a dot to assign (book.pages = 480); brackets come in the next lessons.

steps.title: Add a new field
steps.instructions: Add a new property the object did not have before by assigning to it with dot notation.

steps.title: Print the whole object
steps.instructions: Use console.log to print the object itself, so the changed and added fields are visible.

requirements.title: object literal created
requirements.description: Declares an object with braces. Help: 3.5.4 (Reading and Changing Properties)
requirements.hint: Declare a variable named book and give it an object in braces with at least two name: value pairs.

requirements.title: property read with a dot and printed
requirements.description: console.log prints a property of book read with dot notation, directly or through a variable that is then printed. A print inside a function nobody calls never runs. Help: 3.5.4 (Reading and Changing Properties)
requirements.hint: Inside console.log, reach a property of book with a dot: console.log(book.title). Storing it first (const t = book.title;) and printing t works too. A helper, an alias or a stored result counts too: that is checked when you press Run.

requirements.title: a field changed and a field added
requirements.description: One dot assignment changes a property the object literal of book already had, and another dot assignment adds a property the literal did not have. Help: 3.5.4 (Reading and Changing Properties)
requirements.hint: With a dot for both: change a property the object was built with (book.pages = 480), then add one it did not have (book.author = ...). Square brackets (book["pages"]) come in 3.5.6. Changing the same field twice adds nothing.

requirements.title: whole object printed
requirements.description: Calls console.log. Help: 3.5.4 (Reading and Changing Properties)
requirements.hint: Pass the object itself to console.log (not one property) so the changed and added fields show.

requirements.title: book starts with two or more fields and ends with one more
requirements.description: After the code runs, book is an object with at least three properties: the ones its literal was written with, plus at least one it did not have. Help: 3.5.3 (Example: An Object Literal)
requirements.hint: book must be an object literal with two or more properties. Then add one more by assigning to a name the literal did not have, with a dot: book.year = 1965;

checks.fail: book should be an object literal: const book = { title: "Dune", pages: 412 };
book should end with at least three properties: the two or more you started with, plus the one you added.
book ends with only the fields its literal was written with. Add a new one by assigning to a name the literal did not have: book.year = 1965;

requirements.title: a field of book and the whole object are printed by code that runs
requirements.description: A console.log that runs prints a field read from book (directly, or through a variable that is then printed), and another prints the whole object. Text typed in, a read thrown away, and a print that never runs do not count. Help: 3.5.4 (Reading and Changing Properties)
requirements.hint: Print a field with a dot, console.log(book.title), then the whole object, console.log(book), on lines that run.

checks.fail: Nothing was printed by code that runs. A console.log inside a function nobody calls, or behind a test that is never true, prints nothing.
A printed line says undefined: a read found nothing. Check the spelling of each name you read.
No console.log that runs prints a field read from book. Print it with a dot, console.log(book.title), on a line that runs.
The whole object is not printed by code that runs. Pass book itself to console.log, console.log(book), after the change and the add, so every field shows.
